Consider the following PR description:
Contains.as_set returns Contains
```py
>>> Contains(x, Reals).as_set()
Contains(x, Reals)
```

This is wrong because Contains is not a set (it's a boolean). It results in failures in other places because it doesn't have as_relational (since it isn't a set). For instance, from https://github.com/sympy/sympy/pull/14965#discussion_r205281989

When we call `as_set()` on a boolean expression, it should return the set of values (of the free variable) for which the expression is true. So `Contains(x, Reals).as_set()` should return `Reals`, because the set of x values for which `x ∈ Reals` is true is `Reals`.
